subject: [hw] IV -> V14: T16 CBNZ with i=1 (0xBBxx) is never dispatched; it is the stop after the V34 shims on the vpud path
body:
Host evidence from the real vendor set (V03 loader + V02 core, current tree):

  stop UNDEF insn=0xbbe8 pc=0x4008284e  (vpud base 0x40080000 -> vpud vaddr 0x284e)
  trace: i T 4008284e bbe8 vpud+0x284e   <- the instruction that ends the run

llvm-mc --triple=thumbv7a-linux-gnueabi says `cbnz r0, #0x7a` -> encoding [0xe8,0xbb], so the word is a well-formed T1 CBNZ with Rn=0, imm5=0x1d, i=1, target 0x28cc (llvm-objdump agrees: 284e: bbe8 cbnz r0, 0x28cc).

emu/n2a32_t16.c:324 routes with
    if ((w & 0xF700u) == 0xB100u)  /* CBZ 0xB1xx, CBNZ 0xB9xx */
For 0xBBE8 that is 0xBBE8 & 0xF700 = 0xB300, so it falls through to the reserved-hole N2A32_UNDEF.

Two defects, both in that one line and its helper t16_misc_cbz():
1. The mask must keep bit 9 out (it is the offset LSB `i`, not part of the opcode) but it currently masks bit 11 out too. 0xF500 == 0xB100 accepts 0xB1xx/0xB3xx (CBZ, i=0/1) and 0xB9xx/0xBBxx (CBNZ, i=0/1) and still rejects the rest of 0xBxxx.
2. t16_misc_cbz() computes
       target = c->r[15] + ((w >> 3) & 0x1Fu) << 1
   and ignores bit 9. ARM ARM: imm32 = ZeroExtend(i:imm5:`0`). For 0xBBE8 the offset is 0x7a, not 0x3a; the correct term is ((w >> 9) & 1u) << 6.

Request: fix both, add 0xBBE8 (cbnz r0,#0x7a, taken and not-taken) and 0xB3xx (cbz with i=1) to the V14 tests, and post rev. This is the first stop after V34s shims, so it blocks IV M-c.

Second, separate stop in the same run (reported to hw-v33, not V14): the guest also executes memcpy(dst=0x40000000, src=0xff600000, 0x1000) because V33s fopen fallback opens the HOST /proc/self/maps; the core converts that host SIGSEGV to FAULT at 0xff600000. After the V14 fix the run should reach further; I will post the next stop immediately.
